A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SyncMind/SyncBench research. Their complete main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of seven LLM agents on SyncBench, including independent versus collaborative recovery, resource-constraint experiments, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and their numerical results in Section 4 and Appendices B–C, together with recovery examples in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The recovery procedures, resource-awareness framework, benchmark-construction pipeline, and simulated collaborator design remain unchanged in Sections 2–3. Appendix D retains the same prompts and interaction instructions.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 21 Python repositories and the same Caller and Callee tasks involving outdated testing functions and dependencies. No evaluated dataset, domain, or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain Llama-3.1-8B/70B, Llama-3.3-70B, DeepSeek-V2.5, GPT-4o mini, GPT-4o, and Claude-3.5-Sonnet. The independent/collaborative comparisons and oracle-information experiment also retain their participants.

E3.justification: Both retain the 300-instance evaluation subset, with 150 Caller and 150 Callee instances, identical validation criteria and metrics, 30/50-turn experiments, and the same budget and action-cost settings.

E4.justification: The pilot tests, oracle-information experiment, communication-quality and timing analyses, resource-sensitivity studies, repository comparisons, and success/failure case studies are retained unchanged across the main text and appendices.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies new or revised repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical uncertainty reporting remains unchanged.

E6.justification: The matched tables, plots, and case studies retain their results. For example, Claude-3.5-Sonnet's independent/collaborative success rates remain 28.18%/33.70% in Table C1, and the oracle-information experiment retains 86.33% success.

T1.justification: The formal out-of-sync conditions and recovery criteria in Section 2.1 and metric definitions in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about capability gaps, low collaboration willingness, and limited resource awareness. Minor abstract wording edits do not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: The result interpretations and Appendix A limitations are unchanged, including restrictions to Python repositories with unit tests, imperfect simulation of live collaboration, and simplified resource modeling.

D1.justification: Implementation, environment, cost, and prompting details remain unchanged. The existing code/data website moves from the first-page footnote into the abstract; this supplies no new access information or resource availability.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning in Section 5 are unchanged. Bibliographic additions for Balloli et al., MINT, and OpenHands only complete venue or preprint metadata for already cited works.

P1.justification: v2 adds a funding acknowledgement, updates author affiliations/contact details and publication text, lightly edits the abstract, and completes several references. Section 3.1's benchmark-construction reference is corrected from Appendix B.3 to B.2; the substantive narrative remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Main-text layout and figure placement shift, including Figure 4 changing columns and Question Quality moving within page 7. Question Quality is renumbered from Figure 7 to 8 and Time Allocation from 8 to 7, with matching appendix references updated. Figure content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The corrected appendix reference, completed bibliographic details, and added acknowledgement provide small editorial benefits. Methods, empirical evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged, while the layout adjustments do not establish a meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
